title: Microsoft Copilot: Copilot Code builds software and apps from plain-language descriptions
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing, spending controls and local sandbox policies are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The spending-policy path needs only a minor clarification to include the policy-scope heading.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The General Availability target is December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability", "Preview" ]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "products": [ "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes work grounding by Work IQ.
claims.quote: building through natural language, grounded in their work by Work IQ

claims.claim: Copilot Code is a Code tab in Microsoft Copilot that builds software from plain-language descriptions.
claims.quote: The Code tab in Microsoft Copilot turns what you describe into working software.

claims.claim: Copilot Code shows a live preview.
claims.quote: Copilot Code builds it, shows you a live preview, and iterates with you until it works.

claims.claim: Users can iterate on the software conversationally.
claims.quote: Refine: Describe a change, such as adding a feature, adjusting the layout, or fixing a problem, and Copilot Code updates the project.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists dashboards, internal tools, static websites, data transforms and scripts as examples.
claims.quote: Create apps, dashboards, internal tools, static websites, data transforms, and scripts in plain language.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: With permission, Copilot Code uses the user's Microsoft 365 documents, emails, meetings and calendar as context.
claims.quote: With your permission, Copilot Code uses your Microsoft 365 documents, emails, meetings, and calendar as context.

claims.claim: Apps can be published to Copilot Managed Runtime.
claims.quote: Build and publish apps to Copilot Managed Runtime

claims.claim: Published apps can be shared with people or groups in the organisation.
claims.quote: Ask Code to share it with specific people or groups in your organization and choose if they can use it.

claims.claim: Building does not publish an app; publication is a separate step requested by the user.
claims.quote: Building doesn't publish it—publishing is a separate step that happens only when you ask for it.

claims.claim: Connecting GitHub is optional.
claims.quote: Connecting GitHub is optional—you don't need it to build, preview, and save projects in Copilot Code.

claims.claim: Connected GitHub repositories support creating branches and commits.
claims.quote: Create branches and commits.

claims.claim: Copilot Code can open draft pull requests.
claims.quote: Open a draft pull request with a description of the change.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot Code can push changes to GitHub.
claims.quote: Push changes to GitHub.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents Copilot Code as a preview feature requiring Frontier preview membership.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature provided under Microsoft Product Terms. ... You need to be part of the Frontier preview program to get early access.

claims.claim: Preview behaviour can change before general availability.
claims.quote: As these features are still in development, their availability and capabilities may change over time.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining a Copilot licence with credit-based usage.
claims.quote: Build an app in Copilot Code | A Microsoft Copilot license, plus Copilot Credits billed through a spending policy that includes Copilot Code

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The feature requirements page requires a Microsoft Copilot licence for work accounts.
claims.quote: Work (organization) account | A Microsoft Copilot license, and the Code tab in Microsoft Copilot enabled by your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The requirements page says the organisation must have enabled the Code tab.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Copilot license, and the Code tab in Microsoft Copilot enabled by your organization.

claims.claim: The Managed Runtime licensing page says the Copilot licence does not include Code or Cowork usage.
claims.quote: The license doesn't include Cowork or Code usage, which is billed through Copilot Credits

claims.claim: The Copilot overview specifically requires Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) for usage-based billing capabilities.
claims.quote: To use usage-based billing capabilities, you must have a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

claims.claim: Learn also supports personal Microsoft accounts on a supported Copilot consumer plan.
claims.quote: Personal Microsoft account | A supported Microsoft Copilot consumer plan.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the Code tab itself is on or off by default in a new tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Code" "default" "Code tab" enable. Opened Code requirements, Code admin, Managed Runtime admin overview and usage-based billing management; none states the new-tenant default of the Code tab itself.

claims.claim: Copilot Code can access the local file system.
claims.quote: Copilot Code works inside the project folders on your device ... It can read the files there, install what the project needs, and run the app

claims.claim: Copilot Code can make network connections subject to approval and policy.
claims.quote: Copilot Code asks for your approval before it reaches outside that folder or makes a network connection.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Code uses usage-based billing and requires a spending policy.
claims.quote: Copilot Code is a usage-based billing feature and requires a spending policy to be configured.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is selected by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: An existing spending policy with automatic service coverage can include newly supported Code usage.
claims.quote: Code (Copilot license required) ... Spending policies can automatically apply to future supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents.

claims.claim: Organizational Data in Copilot Code defaults to on for cloud sessions and off for local sessions.
claims.quote: Organizational Data in Copilot Code | On for cloud; Off for local

claims.claim: Sharing an app does not share its underlying data.
claims.quote: Sharing an app doesn’t share its underlying data.

claims.claim: Recipients see only data they already have permission to access in connected sources.
claims.quote: People you share with see only the data they already have permission to access in connected sources

claims.claim: Recipients may need to approve a connection on first opening the app.
claims.quote: might be asked to approve a connection the first time they open the app.

claims.claim: Managed Runtime apps inherit default environment group settings for connectors, sharing and external content.
claims.quote: Every app inherits the default environment group settings, which control what it can connect to, who it can be shared with, and what external content it can load.

claims.claim: For organisational use, a Microsoft Entra work account is the required sign-in.
claims.quote: For work accounts, a Microsoft Entra (work) account is the default and only required sign-in.

claims.claim: The GitHub connection policy defaults to off.
claims.quote: GitHub connection | Off | This policy setting controls whether users can connect a GitHub account in Copilot Code.

claims.claim: The administrator must enable GitHub use in Copilot Code.
claims.quote: Your system administrator must enable working with GitHub in Copilot Code.

claims.claim: Allowed Github Connections list defaults to Both.
claims.quote: Allowed Github Connections list | Both

claims.claim: By default Copilot Code requests permission before network calls.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot Code asks for permission to: ... Make network calls, including accessing the internet.

claims.claim: By default it requests permission before using extensions and MCP.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot Code asks for permission to: ... Use extensions and MCP.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: By default it requests permission before running shell or terminal commands.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot Code asks for permission to: ... Run shell or terminal commands.

claims.claim: By default it requests permission for file access outside projects and folders already in use.
claims.quote: Read or write files outside the projects and folders already in use in Copilot Code.

claims.claim: The Auto-approve setting is on by default.
claims.quote: Auto-approve setting | On

claims.claim: That policy lets users allow automatic approvals rather than confirming each action.
claims.quote: This policy setting controls whether users can let Copilot auto-approve permissions in Copilot Code instead of confirming each action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Always allow remains enabled until the user disables it.
claims.quote: When you enable Always allow, it remains enabled until you disable it.

claims.claim: The local sandbox is required on managed devices when its policy is unconfigured.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, the sandbox is required and users can't turn it off. ... On managed devices with no policy set, the sandbox stays on

claims.claim: The device sandbox policies do not affect cloud agent sessions.
claims.quote: This policy doesn't affect Copilot Code Cloud agent sessions.

claims.claim: The sandbox does not restrict a generated app run outside a Copilot Code session.
claims.quote: If you run an app that Copilot Code built outside of a Copilot Code session, the Sandbox doesn't restrict it.

claims.claim: The local sandbox supports Windows 11 version 24H2 or later.
claims.quote: The sandbox works on Windows 11, version 24H2 or later, and on Mac.

claims.claim: The local sandbox supports Mac.
claims.quote: Mac | Supported.

claims.claim: Windows 10 does not support the sandbox.
claims.quote: Windows 10 | Not supported.

claims.claim: Users whose devices do not support the sandbox can run projects in the cloud.
claims.quote: If your organization requires the Sandbox and your device doesn't support it, you can still run projects in the cloud.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each app user needs Power Apps Premium or coverage through a spending policy including Copilot Managed Runtime.
claims.quote: To run the app, each user need either a Power Apps Premium license or inclusion in a spending policy with Copilot Managed Runtime.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Code usage is metered in Copilot Credits through a spending policy.
claims.quote: Build an app in Copilot Code | A Microsoft Copilot license, plus Copilot Credits billed through a spending policy that includes Copilot Code

claims.claim: Spending policies are limits rather than purchases and do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limits, not purchases. A policy doesn't reserve or allocate credits to anyone

claims.claim: Customers pay for actual consumption.
claims.quote: you pay only for what is actually consumed.

claims.claim: Microsoft says building is the most credit-intensive part of the app lifecycle.
claims.quote: Building is the most credit-intensive part of the lifecycle

claims.claim: Microsoft advises sizing build limits separately from runtime limits.
claims.quote: so size build limits separately from runtime limits.

claims.claim: Managed Runtime charges 0.1 Copilot Credits per API call for credit-billed app use.
claims.quote: Credits are consumed by the API calls an app makes, at 0.1 Copilot Credits per call (1 credit covers 10 API calls).

claims.claim: Specialised services such as Work IQ APIs are charged separately at their own rates.
claims.quote: Apps that use specialized services, like Work IQ APIs, are charged separately at their own rates.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: A specific credit rate for building with Copilot Code is not published in the reviewed documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Code" "credit" "rate" building licensing. Opened Code requirements, Code admin, Managed Runtime licensing-credits and usage-based billing overview; search also returned licensing-faq. No Code build rate was stated.

claims.claim: The reviewed pages do not state what the roadmap's GA target changes about licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Code" "General Availability" licensing Frontier. Opened Code overview, requirements, admin and Managed Runtime licensing-credits; no GA-specific licensing transition is stated.

claims.claim: Windows x64 and Arm are supported through the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.
claims.quote: Windows | Supported (x64 and Arm), in the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.

claims.claim: Mac is supported in the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.
claims.quote: Mac | Supported (Intel and Apple silicon), in the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.

claims.claim: Cloud development is supported on the web at https://m365.cloud.microsoft.
claims.quote: Web | Supported for cloud development at https://m365.cloud.microsoft.

claims.claim: iOS, iPadOS and Android support cloud sessions in the mobile app.
claims.quote: iOS and iPadOS | Supported for cloud sessions, in the Microsoft Copilot mobile app. ... Android | Supported for cloud sessions, in the Microsoft Copilot mobile app.

claims.claim: Local sessions are unavailable on mobile.
claims.quote: Local sessions aren't available on mobile.

claims.claim: Building and publishing to Copilot Managed Runtime is documented as preview.
claims.quote: Building and publishing apps to Copilot Managed Runtime is a preview feature

claims.claim: Each Managed Runtime app appears in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Each app appears in the Microsoft 365 admin center, where you can track usage, monitor health, and manage its lifecycle.

claims.claim: Only users covered by a Copilot Code spending policy can build apps with it.
claims.quote: Only users who are included in a spending policy for Copilot Code can build apps with it.

claims.claim: Consumption can be reviewed in Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management.
claims.quote: Use Copilot > Cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center to review consumption by policy, service, and user, and adjust limits.

claims.claim: The printed spending-policy wizard path reaches group scope, service selection and the limits section.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... Define the policy scope ... Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.
claims.fix: Insert the documented heading after '+ Add spending policy': 'Copilot > Cost management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Define the policy scope > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Copilot Code > Set limits and alerts'. The remaining labels are supported by this page and the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/apps/licensing-credits.

claims.claim: Copilot Code is a selectable service in a maker spending policy.
claims.quote: Create or edit a user-based spending policy that includes the makers, or a security group that contains them, and select Copilot Cowork and Copilot Code.

claims.claim: The wizard supports Specific groups and monthly per-user limits under Set limits and alerts.
claims.quote: switch to Specific groups and select the directory group. ... Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy with the specified limits and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: The create API requires displayName and a concrete @odata.type as well as periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete @odata.type. Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: A policy created by the API starts disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: The API example uses serviceId cowork and workIQ rather than a Copilot Code identifier.
claims.quote: "serviceSettings": [ { "serviceId": "cowork", "state": "enabled" }, { "serviceId": "workIQ", "state": "enabled" } ]

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through Graph requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The spending-policy API is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The Intune imported-template profile route followed by Microsoft Copilot > Code Tab locates the documented device policies.
claims.quote: import the policy file (windows/admx/copilotapp.admx). For more information ... Import custom ADMX and ADML administrative templates into Microsoft Intune. ... Policy location: Microsoft Copilot > Code Tab.

claims.claim: The Intune portion uses Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy, Windows 10 and later, Templates > Imported Administrative templates (Preview), Create and Configuration settings.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. ... Platform: Select Windows 10 and later. ... Templates > Imported Administrative templates (Preview) ... Select Create. ... In Configuration settings, select and configure the settings

claims.claim: The documented macOS policy keys are CopilotDeviceCodeTabSandboxEnabled and CopilotDeviceCodeTabOutboundNetworkAccessMode in com.microsoft.Copilot.
claims.quote: Domain: com.microsoft.Copilot. ... Copilot sandbox required ... CopilotDeviceCodeTabSandboxEnabled ... Copilot sandbox outbound network access mode ... CopilotDeviceCodeTabOutboundNetworkAccessMode

claims.claim: Windows administrators must import the Copilot policy templates before configuring their Code Tab settings.
claims.quote: Download the Microsoft Copilot policy templates, then import the policy file (windows/admx/copilotapp.admx). ... Configure the policies - Policy location: Microsoft Copilot > Code Tab.

claims.claim: The named organisation-level Code feature policies have no documented admin-centre path or API, apart from the separately documented device preinstall policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Code" "GitHub connection" "Organizational Data" policy configure admin API Graph; "Copilot Code" "Auto-approve" "Graph" policy API; "Copilot Code" "Pre-install" "execution location" configure policy. Read Code admin and Copilot settings; no such routes or calls.

claims.claim: Execution location policy can restrict local or cloud agent sessions, and spending policies limit Code access and usage.
claims.quote: This policy setting controls where Copilot Code can run agent sessions: on the user's device, in the cloud, or both. ... Copilot Code honors the usage and budget limits you set.

claims.claim: Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access to eligible previews by user or group.
claims.quote: Copilot Frontier | Choose which users or groups can access eligible preview features. | Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier.

claims.claim: Learn says Copilot Code audit logs exist and are accessible to IT administrators.
claims.quote: Copilot Code logs the actions it takes so you can review them. IT administrators can access audit logs

claims.claim: The Code administration page supplies no location or event names for its code, command and file-action audit logs.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Code" audit logs event names Purview. Read Code admin in full and Purview audit-copilot search excerpts. Code admin lists generated code, commands and file actions but gives no log location or event identifiers for those Code actions.
